claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me begin with a few key questions.

**First, could you please tell me the name and date of birth of each child you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who was born in March 2008, so they're 16 now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who was born in March 2008 and is currently 16 years old.

I need to gather a bit more information to assess your eligibility. 

**Are you, or Alex, a British citizen, or do you have settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training, or has Alex left school/training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left school recently, but they've just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's useful context.

**Is Alex currently registered with the careers service as unemployed, or are they in any form of employment or training scheme at the moment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they registered with the careers service as unemployed - they're trying to work out their next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question:

**What is your residency status? Are you a UK resident, and have you been living in the UK for at least the last 2 years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester. I've been living here for years, well over 2 years.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review the situation:

- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- You have been a UK resident for well over 2 years
- Your child Alex was born in March 2008 and is now 16 years old
- Alex has recently left school and is registered with the careers service as unemployed

Based on the Child Benefit rules, a child can continue to receive Child Benefit after age 16 if they are:
- In full-time education, or
- In approved training, or
- Registered as unemployed with the careers service and under 18

Since Alex is registered as unemployed with the careers service and is currently 16 (under 18), they meet the eligibility criteria for continuing to receive Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:

- **Your eligibility as a claimant:** You are a British citizen and have been living in the UK for well over 2 years, which meets the residency requirements.

- **Alex's eligibility:** Although Alex has left school, they are still eligible for Child Benefit because they are registered as unemployed with the careers service and are currently 16 years old. This continuation of benefit for young people aged 16-17 is permitted when they're registered unemployed while seeking work or training.

You should be able to proceed with your claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim through the appropriate government channels.
